title: Questionnaire Component & Auth Mode Refactor
why: Users need a reusable question-input component for the AI to collect information interactively. The existing auth mode pattern (yes/no + instructions) should be extracted into a generic questionnaire component that supports multiple prompt modes. This avoids duplicating the interaction pattern and enables interviews, structured data collection, and UX-friendly user input throughout the application.
outcomes: A reusable Questionnaire component supporting yes/no, radio, checkbox, and free-text prompt modes. The auth mode is refactored to use this component. The tool accepts an array of questions and returns structured answers. Consistent keyboard navigation (Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter) across all modes.

milestones.name: Questionnaire Domain Model
milestones.objective: Define the domain types for question types, question structure, and answer structure that the tool and UI will share.
milestones.success: QuestionType enum, Question struct, Answer struct compile and are importable by both the tool handler and the UI component.
milestones.diagram: QuestionType(yesno|radio|checkbox|text) → Question(id, type, prompt, options, required) → Answer(id, value, instructions) → QuestionnaireResult(answers array)

tasks.name: Add QuestionType enum
tasks.what: Add QuestionType enum with YesNo, Radio, Checkbox, Text constants in internal/domain/questionnaire.go.
tasks.why: Single source of truth for supported prompt modes, used by both tool schema validation and UI rendering.
acceptance: Enum compiles, Valid() returns true for known types and false for unknown

tasks.name: Add Question struct
tasks.what: Add Question struct with ID, Type, Prompt, Options, Required fields in internal/domain/questionnaire.go.
tasks.why: Represents a single question sent by the AI tool, carrying all metadata needed for rendering and validation.
acceptance: Struct compiles, HasOptions returns true for radio/checkbox, SupportsInstructions always true

tasks.name: Add Answer struct
tasks.what: Add Answer struct with ID, Value (interface{}), Instructions fields in internal/domain/questionnaire.go.
tasks.why: Carries the user's response back to the AI. Value is interface{} to handle string (yesno/radio/text) or []string (checkbox).
acceptance: Struct compiles, Answer.Value is interface{} to support multiple types

milestones.name: Questionnaire UI Component
milestones.objective: Build the core QuestionnairePrompt UI component that renders questions sequentially, handles keyboard navigation between answer selection and text input, and collects structured answers.
milestones.success: QuestionnairePrompt renders questions one at a time, supports all four prompt modes with keyboard navigation (Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter), and produces a QuestionnaireResult on completion.
milestones.diagram: QuestionnairePrompt → iterates Questions → renders current Question → sub-component per type (YesNoPrompt / RadioPrompt / CheckboxPrompt / TextPrompt) → Tab switches to InstructionsInput → Shift+Tab returns to selector → Enter advances to next or submits

tasks.name: Add QuestionnairePrompt struct
tasks.what: Create QuestionnairePrompt struct in internal/ui/questionnaire.go with Questions, currentIndex, answers slice, textMode flag, and instructionBuffer.
tasks.why: Manages state across a multi-question flow: tracks current question, accumulated answers, and whether the user is in answer-selection or instruction-input mode.
acceptance: Struct compiles, NewQuestionnairePrompt initializes correctly, IsComplete returns true when all questions answered

tasks.name: Implement QuestionnairePrompt Render
tasks.what: Add Render() method to QuestionnairePrompt that delegates to per-type renderers and shows progress indicator.
tasks.why: Displays the current question with appropriate input UI, progress bar, and navigation hints.
acceptance: Render outputs progress, prompt, answer block, and navigation hint. Delegates correctly per question type.

tasks.name: Implement YesNo renderer
tasks.what: Add renderYesNo method that shows [Y]es / [N]o with selection highlight on current choice.
tasks.why: YesNo is the simplest mode and the basis for auth mode reuse. Selected option gets highlight style.
acceptance: Yes/No render with highlight on selected option

tasks.name: Implement Radio renderer
tasks.what: Add renderRadio method that lists options with index numbers, highlights selected.
tasks.why: Single-select from a list of options. Each option gets a number prefix for keyboard navigation.
acceptance: Options render with numbered prefixes, selected option highlighted

tasks.name: Implement Checkbox renderer
tasks.what: Add renderCheckbox method with toggle selection (space to toggle each option), shows checked/unchecked state.
tasks.why: Multi-select from a list. Each option can be independently toggled. Selection tracked as a set of indices.
acceptance: Options show ☐/☑ state, selection tracked in checkedItems map

tasks.name: Implement Text input renderer
tasks.what: Add renderTextInput that shows a dedicated inline text field for free-text answers, distinct from the shared textarea.
tasks.why: Free-text questions need their own input area scoped to this single question. Not the global textarea — a focused inline input with cursor.
acceptance: Text input renders inline with cursor indicator, placeholder when empty. Instruction input separate from question text.

tasks.name: Implement QuestionnairePrompt key handler
tasks.what: Add HandleKey(msg tea.KeyMsg) method that processes navigation (←→, Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Backspace, Runes) per question type.
tasks.why: Routes keyboard input to the correct action based on current question type and text mode. Core interaction logic for the component.
acceptance: Key handler processes all modes correctly. submitCurrent builds the right Answer type per question. Advances index on submit.

tasks.name: Implement Radio and Checkbox key handlers
tasks.what: Add handleRadioKey (←→ navigate, Enter submit, Tab instructions) and handleCheckboxKey (←→ navigate, Space toggle, Enter submit, Tab instructions).
tasks.why: Radio navigates with arrows and submits single selection. Checkbox navigates with arrows, toggles with space, and submits all checked items.
acceptance: Radio navigates with arrows, checkbox toggles with space and navigates with arrows, both support Tab for instructions and Enter to submit

milestones.name: Questionnaire Tool
milestones.objective: Register the questionnaire tool with the tool registry, defining its JSON schema (array of questions in, array of answers out) and execution handler that pauses for user input.
milestones.success: Tool is registered, accepts a batch of questions, pauses the stream in ModeQuestionnaire, and returns structured answers to the AI.
milestones.diagram: LLM calls questionnaire({questions: [...]}) → schema validates → execute pauses stream → sets ModeQuestionnaire → QuestionnairePrompt renders → user answers → tool returns {answers: [...]} → stream resumes

tasks.name: Register questionnaire tool with schema
tasks.what: Create internal/tools/questionnaire.go with JSON schema defining the questions array parameter and register it in the tool registry.
tasks.why: The AI needs a tool definition to call. Schema enforces question structure (id, type, prompt, optional options).
snippet:
package tools

import "squid-os/internal/domain"

var Questionnaire = Tool{
	Name:        "questionnaire",\n\tDescription: "Ask the user a series of questions and collect structured answers. Supports yesno, radio, checkbox, and text question types.",
	Schema: ,
	IsDestructive: func(args map[string]interface{}) bool { return false },
	Execute:       executeQuestionnaire,
}
acceptance: Schema is valid JSON, tool is non-destructive, registered in tool registry

tasks.name: Implement questionnaire Execute handler
tasks.what: Add executeQuestionnaire that parses questions from args, stores them on the stream for the UI to pick up, and returns ToolResult with status indicating user interaction needed.
tasks.why: Unlike normal tools, questionnaire doesn't produce an immediate result — it pauses the stream and defers to the UI component. The execute handler sets up the questionnaire context and signals the stream to pause.
acceptance: Execute validates questions, returns ResultStatusPending with Questionnaire populated

milestones.name: Stream Integration
milestones.objective: Integrate the questionnaire into the stream loop as a new mode (ModeQuestionnaire), handling the pause/resume cycle and wiring it into the key event dispatch.
milestones.success: When the questionnaire tool is called, the stream pauses in ModeQuestionnaire, the QuestionnairePrompt renders, user answers all questions, and the stream resumes with the structured result injected as a tool response.
milestones.diagram: stream → tool_calls → questionnaire returns Pending → set ModeQuestionnaire → init QuestionnairePrompt → render loop → user keys → HandleKey → submitCurrent per question → all complete → build ToolResult with answers JSON → resume stream

tasks.name: Add ModeQuestionnaire to modes
tasks.what: Add ModeQuestionnaire to the Mode enum in internal/app/modes.go and its String() method.
tasks.why: New mode for the questionnaire interaction flow, distinct from ModeAuthorize.
acceptance: ModeQuestionnaire compiles, String() returns "questionnaire"

tasks.name: Add questionnaire context to streamState
tasks.what: Add questionnairePrompt *ui.QuestionnairePrompt and questionnaireToolCall partialTool to streamState in stream.go.
tasks.why: The stream needs to hold the questionnaire UI state and know which tool call to resolve upon completion.
acceptance: streamState holds questionnaire context, setQuestionnaireMode initializes it from questions

tasks.name: Detect questionnaire tool in executeTools
tasks.what: In executeTools, check if the current partial is the questionnaire tool returning Pending. If so, call setQuestionnaireMode and return nil to pause the stream.
tasks.why: The stream needs to intercept the questionnaire's pending result and switch to the questionnaire mode instead of treating it as a normal tool result.
acceptance: When questionnaire tool returns Pending, stream enters ModeQuestionnaire instead of continuing

tasks.name: Render questionnaire in View and wire key dispatch
tasks.what: In render.go View(), add case for ModeQuestionnaire that renders questionnairePrompt. In update.go handleKey, add case for ModeQuestionnaire that routes to questionnairePrompt.HandleKey and handles completion.
tasks.why: Wires the questionnaire into the main View/Update cycle. On completion (IsComplete), resolves the tool call with the answers JSON and resumes the stream.
acceptance: Questionnaire renders in View, key events route through HandleKey, on completion resolves with answers JSON and resumes stream

milestones.name: Auth Mode Refactor
milestones.objective: Refactor the authorization mode (from tool-authorization plan) to use the questionnaire component instead of its own yes/no + instructions UI. The auth mode becomes a thin wrapper that builds a single-question questionnaire and interprets the result.
milestones.success: ModeAuthorize uses the questionnaire component with a single yesno question. The existing AuthorizationContext maps to a Question/Answer pair. No duplicated UI code.
milestones.diagram: ModeAuthorize → builds QuestionnairePrompt with single yesno question("Proceed with <tool>?") → user answers yes/no + optional instructions → resolveAuthorization maps Answer.Value (bool) + Answer.Instructions to AuthResult

tasks.name: Replace AuthorizationPrompt with QuestionnairePrompt for auth mode
tasks.what: In setAuthMode(), replace the old ui.AuthorizationPrompt initialization with a QuestionnairePrompt containing a single yesno question. Update ModeAuthorize rendering to use the questionnaire prompt.
tasks.why: Eliminates code duplication — auth mode reuses the same questionnaire component instead of maintaining its own yes/no + instructions UI.
acceptance: setAuthMode initializes a questionnaire with a single yesno question. ModeAuthorize renders via questionnairePrompt

tasks.name: Wire ModeAuthorize key handling through questionnaire
tasks.what: In handleKey, update ModeAuthorize case to use questionnairePrompt.HandleKey. On completion, map the questionnaire answer to AuthResult and call the existing resolveAuthorization.
tasks.why: Auth mode key handling now goes through the questionnaire component. On completion, the boolean answer maps to Accepted/Rejected and instructions map to WithInstructions variants.
acceptance: ModeAuthorize key handling goes through questionnaire. On completion, answer maps correctly to the 4 AuthResult variants. resolveAuthorization receives the mapped result.

tasks.name: Remove old AuthorizationPrompt struct
tasks.what: Delete internal/ui/authorization.go (or deprecate the AuthorizationPrompt struct) since its functionality is now subsumed by the questionnaire component.
tasks.why: Eliminates the duplicated yes/no + instructions UI. Auth mode now purely uses the questionnaire component.

milestones.name: System Prompt Update
milestones.objective: Add instructions to the system prompt explaining the questionnaire tool — when to use it, how to structure questions, and how to interpret answers.
milestones.success: System prompt includes a questionnaire tool section explaining all four question types with examples.
milestones.diagram: sys-prompt.go → DefaultAssistantPrompt() adds questionnaire section → explains types (yesno, radio, checkbox, text) → explains answer format

tasks.name: Add questionnaire tool instructions to system prompt
tasks.what: Add a questionnaire tool section to the default system prompt in internal/config/sys-prompt.go explaining when and how to use it.
tasks.why: The LLM needs to know when to use the questionnaire tool (interviews, structured data collection, confirmation) and how to format questions properly.
snippet:
## Questionnaire Tool
- Use the questionnaire tool when you need to collect structured information from the user through an interactive interview.
- Question types:
  - yesno: Simple yes/no question. Answer returns a boolean.
  - radio: Single selection from a list. Provide options array. Answer returns the selected option string.
  - checkbox: Multiple selection from a list. Provide options array. Answer returns an array of selected option strings.
  - text: Free-text answer. Answer returns a string.
- Each question must have a unique id, type, and prompt.
- For radio/checkbox, provide an options array with the available choices.
- The user can add optional instructions/notes to any answer.
- Answers are returned as {"answers": [{"id": "...", "value": ..., "instructions": "..."}]}
- Use this for interviews, onboarding, configuration, or any multi-step information gathering.
acceptance: System prompt contains questionnaire instructions with all four types and usage guidelines
